## About

panzoom takes every Python (Jupyter) figure lightbox would take on its own, so
no figure needs to be marked. lightbox is on too, but only cells that ask for it
with lightbox options open in it ([case 4](#c4)). The same cases open in
lightbox alone on [lightbox on the Python cases](j-jupyter-lightbox.html), and
the R cases are on [panzoom on every image](c-panzoom-auto.html).

```yaml
filters:
  - panzoom
panzoom: true
lightbox: true
```

Jupyter leaves the `panzoom` and `lightbox` options out of the code shown on the
page. The **Code** button at the top shows the full source.

The plots share this setup:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 400)
```

## 1. Figure with a caption {#c1 expect-open="panzoom"}

A Python figure with a caption. It opens in panzoom.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a sine wave"
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(x))
plt.show()
```

## 2. Plot without a caption {#c2 expect-open="panzoom"}

A plot without a caption. It opens in panzoom.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a cosine wave"

plt.plot(x, np.cos(x))
plt.show()
```

## 3. Subfigures {#c3 expect-open="panzoom"}

One cell with two plots, made subfigures by `fig-subcap`. Either one opens in
panzoom, in a two-image gallery.

```{python}
#| label: fig-pair
#| fig-cap: "Sine and cosine, from one cell."
#| fig-subcap: ["Sine", "Cosine"]
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Line plot of a sine wave"
#|   - "Line plot of a cosine wave"
#| layout-ncol: 2

plt.plot(x, np.sin(2 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(2 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 4. lightbox options {#c4 expect-open="glightbox"}

One cell with two plots and `lightbox:` options for a group and a description.
Asking for lightbox keeps the cell out of panzoom, as in cases 6 and 7 of
[panzoom on every image](c-panzoom-auto.html). With Jupyter, lightbox ignores
these options, so each plot opens in lightbox on its own, without the group or
description.

```{python}
#| lightbox:
#|   group: waves
#|   description: "Ignored by lightbox with Jupyter."
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Line plot of a sine wave"
#|   - "Line plot of a cosine wave"

plt.plot(x, np.sin(3 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(3 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 5. lightbox off {#c5 expect-open="nothing"}

A cell with `lightbox: false`. panzoom leaves a cell's own lightbox setting
alone, so clicking the plot does nothing.

```{python}
#| lightbox: false
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a sine wave"
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave, from a cell with `lightbox: false`."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 6. panzoom on a cell {#c6 expect-open="panzoom"}

A cell with `#| panzoom: true`. It opens in panzoom, ahead of the document's
`lightbox: true`.

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of a cosine wave"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "A cosine wave, from a cell with `panzoom: true`."

plt.plot(x, np.cos(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 7. Markdown image {#c7 expect-open="panzoom"}

A markdown image alone in a paragraph. It opens in panzoom.

```markdown {.show-source}
![Chilmark beach at sunset.](../../images/mv-0.jpg){fig-alt="Sunset over a sandy beach, with a tall rock stack against the sun"}
```

## 8. Opt out of lightbox {#c8 expect-open="nothing"}

A markdown image with `.nolightbox`. panzoom only takes images lightbox would,
so clicking it does nothing.

```markdown {.show-source}
![Aquinnah, kept out with `.nolightbox`.](../../images/mv-1.jpg){.nolightbox fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah"}
```
